newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken not aware of govt sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken not aware of govt sale plans.

text.p: Swedish state-controlled Nordbanken's management on Friday said it had not been informed about any plans by the government to sell the state's 58 percent stake in the bank at the present moment.
"We have not been informed about anything special going on right now," Lars G Nordstrom, vice president of Nordbanken, told Reuters.
"The government has previously said it will sell its stake in Nordbanken when the timing is right."

Speculation about a sale was fuelled by an article in business daily Dagens Industri which said the government was expected to sell 20-25 percent of its stake to Investor AB, the investment vehicle of Sweden's leading finance family, the Wallenbergs.
Such a deal could pave the way for Nordbanken to merge with S-E-Banken, in which the Wallenbergs hold 15 percent of the equity and 16 percent of the votes, the paper said.
Nordstrom at Nordbanken said the bank's management would probably be informed when a sale was in the cards.
He emphasised that Nordbanken will not interfere with a future sale of the state's holding.
He also said the market has to be aware that speculation about different players discussing the deal will turn up now and then.
"But we do not comment on such speculation," he said.
